rationale:
The example gives a concrete case. It uses the source `const A: &str = "éhit"; const B: &str = "hit hit";` and the query `hit`. It expects a complete page with one entry per declaration. Each entry has a tag, node, file, selector and excerpt. `const[A]` has the excerpt `const A: &str = "éhit";`. `const[B]` has the excerpt `const B: &str = "hit hit";`, which is one entry even though it has two hits.

The test `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs` is marked `{test}` for this example. It checks each outcome:
- It writes exactly that source to `code.rs`. It then calls `search_text("hit")` through `ProjectSources` and checks the raw hits. The hits are `const[A]` at 19..22 and `const[B]` at 42..45 and 46..49. This shows that B has two hits.
- It dispatches `search_text` with `{"pattern":"hit"}` through `SessionTools`. It asserts `page["complete"] == true`.
- It asserts that `page["matches"]` equals exactly two entries, tags `"1"` and `"2"`. These carry the interned nodes of `const[A]` and `const[B]`, file `code.rs`, selectors `const[A]` and `const[B]`, and the two excerpts above.
  - This covers one entry per enclosing item (`group_hits`).
  - It covers the page-local tags and the node references.
  - It covers the excerpts. With the default 128-byte window they are clipped to the item span (`windows`). B's two hits merge into one contiguous `hit hit`. The multibyte `é` is preserved.
- It reads the second entry with `read_node` and checks the dependency. It then finishes the search with `used:[]` and with `["2"]`, and checks the recorded dependency on `const[B]`. This shows the tag accounts for use of the excerpt.

One difference remains between the example and the test. The example shows a page after the first-search instructions were delivered, so it has no `instructions` key. The test's search is the first in its session, so the page carries the instructions. The test checks only `complete` and `matches`, so this does not affect the example's outcomes. The omission of instructions on later pages is covered by other tests, for example `search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot`. The tests adequately check the example.

text: For the same `hit` query, the agent receives one excerpt per declaration. After the first-search instructions have been delivered, the complete page looks like this.

Deliver one entry per enclosing item in a text search, even when the item has several hits. Group before pagination so an item's excerpt stays together. Each entry carries a node reference under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.node_reference`, one excerpt, and the page-local tag used by `finish_search`. The tag accounts for use of the excerpt. The node reference lets the agent read the full item.

The agent's `search_text` tool accepts a nonnegative `window_bytes`, defaulting to 128. For a hit with byte span `[start, end)`, retain the hit and up to `window_bytes` of source immediately before `start` and after `end`. Clip the window to the enclosing item's span. Move a context boundary that splits a UTF-8 character inward to the nearest character boundary. With `window_bytes: 0`, only the hit spans and the available header and trailer contribute source to the excerpt.

Compute windows for all hits in the item from the same snapshot. Where windows touch or overlap, emit the contiguous source once. This preserves each hit and the text between nearby hits, including whitespace and newlines.
